description.describe_ch: 本課程介紹公共關係實踐。 它旨在讓學生基本了解如何研究溝通問題並在考慮其法律和道德背景的同時制定適當的計劃。
description.describe_eh: This course is an introduction to public relations practice. It is designed to give students a fundamental understanding of how to research a communication problem and develop an appropriate program while considering its legal and ethical contexts.

gradeRules.evalb_memo_en: 20% of the grade is divided weekly, four hours each.

The hallmark of this course is the "Case Method." To thrive, students must transition from passive observers to active stakeholders in the global boardroom. The following pillars define excellence in our classroom:

I. The Architecture of Preparation
Analytical Rigor: Mastery of the case begins long before the session. Students are expected to deconstruct the narrative, identify latent tensions, and command the data within the text.

Evidence-Based Persuasion: Every assertion must be anchored. High-level discourse relies on the synthesis of case facts, foundational theories, and contemporary global data.

II. Dynamic Discourse & Strategic Listening
Active Intellectual Presence: Beyond simple attendance, students must drive the dialogue forward by offering nuanced insights and transformative solutions to global dilemmas.

Generative Listening: Elite communication requires the ability to map the room. Listen with the intent to synthesize—building upon or pivotally reframing the contributions of your peers.

Constructive Friction: We value the "respectful challenge." Promoting a culture of rigorous dissent ensures that every idea is stress-tested through professional, high-level debate.

III. Impact & Equity
Quality over Volubility: In negotiation, brevity is power. We prioritize high-impact, well-reasoned interventions over frequent but superficial commentary.

Democratic Contribution: Lead by creating space. True leaders manage the energy of the room, ensuring a balanced exchange where diverse viewpoints are integrated into the final resolution.

Consistency of Excellence: Impact is measured across the arc of the semester. Intellectual leadership is a sustained commitment, not an occasional performance.

IV. Collaborative Reflexivity
Syndicate Synergy: Negotiation is rarely a solo sport. Excellence is found in the ability to brainstorm and co-create strategic frameworks within small-group dynamics.

Metacognitive Growth: Students should continuously audit their own performance, identifying shifts in their persuasive style and refining their approach to cross-cultural conflict.

Presentation 

Narrative Arc: Structure presentations with a powerful beginning, middle, and end.

Unmediated Presence: Command the room without relying on digital devices or scripts.

Designer’s Mindset: Use impactful visuals and minimal text; avoid cluttered slides.

Authentic Rigor: Provide full references and respect strict time limits.

Resilience: Arrive early to neutralize potential technological glitches.

gradeRuleDescribe.tpa_score_new_en:
Your grade is a holistic assessment of your professional contribution across these six pillars:
  • Presence & Punctuality: Consistent attendance is paramount; regular and timely arrival is a baseline requirement.
  • Strategic Interaction: Active, critical engagement in classroom discussions is the heartbeat of this course.
  • Syndicate Collaboration: Effective and constructive participation during group activities is essential.
  • Presentation Artistry: Demonstrate mastery by avoiding reliance on mobile devices; engagement must be direct and unmediated.
  • Intellectual Preparedness: Arrive having fully mastered all assigned readings to ensure informed contributions.
  • Contribution Quality: Prioritize the depth and impact of your insights over the frequency of speech.
gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol_en:
Intellectual Originality: All work must be your own; plagiarism or uncredited AI usage constitutes a breach of our core academic trust and the covenant of scholarship.

Ethical Dialogue: We thrive on diverse perspectives. All interactions must be characterized by radical respect, fostering a space where ideas are challenged but individuals are always valued.

Technological Resilience: Arrive early to ensure full technological and environmental preparedness. In a globalized digital economy, your ability to troubleshoot is part of your professional reputation.

Adaptive Agility: The global landscape shifts daily. Students are expected to integrate real-time geopolitical events into their analyses, demonstrating the flexibility required to negotiate in a volatile, uncertain world.
gradeRuleDescribe.course_rem_en: Negotiate tomorrow’s news with today’s curiosity. The global headlines you read this morning are the volatile variables you will be forced to navigate at the bargaining table this afternoon. Stay sharp, stay informed, and always lead with empathy.
gradeRuleDescribe.ais_meno_en:
Intellectual Originality: All assignments and discussions must reflect original thought; plagiarism or unauthorized use of AI is a breach of the core academic covenant.

Presence & Punctuality: Consistent attendance and timely arrival are mandatory to honor the collective learning process and maximize engagement.

Proactive Preparedness: Students must master all assigned case studies before class to ensure every contribution is substantive and well-informed.

Ethical Engagement: Participation must be characterized by respectful dialogue and a commitment to the honest exchange of diverse ideas.
